hallucinations.claim: Used `--media-control-bar-background` as the CSS custom property to set the control bar's background, written in Rung 3 as `style={{ "--media-control-bar-background": "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)" } as React.CSSProperties}` on `<MuxPlayer>`.
hallucinations.reality: Neither Mux Player nor its underlying Media Chrome library publishes a `--media-control-bar-background` variable. The closest real variable is `--media-control-background` (and the gerwig theme actually paints the bar with a `::before` gradient). Verified by grepping the published `@mux/mux-player@3.12.0` `dist/` (zero matches for `--media-control-bar-background`) and against Media Chrome's styling reference at https://www.media-chrome.org/docs/en/reference/styling.
hallucinations.evidence: Rung 3 transcript line 2 (Edit tool): `style={{ "--media-control-bar-background": "rgba(0, 0, 0, 0.5)" } as React.CSSProperties}`. After running the page Claude observed `controlBarBgComputed: null` and then conceded "Mux Player's theme doesn't use `--media-control-bar-background`" before switching to `::part(control-bar)`.

notes: Across the five rungs the agent's use of the @mux/mux-player-react surface (default import, props `playbackId`, `streamType`, `muted`, `loop`, `autoPlay`, `poster`, `accentColor`, `theme`), the `image.mux.com` poster URL, the `::part(control-bar bottom)` and `::part(fullscreen button)` selectors, and the Media Chrome CSS variables used in the final yt-theme template (`--media-primary-color`, `--media-secondary-color`, `--media-accent-color`, `--media-control-background`, `--media-control-hover-background`, `--media-text-color`, `--media-tooltip-display`, `--media-control-padding`, `--media-font-family`, `--media-font-size`, and the `--media-range-*` family) all check out against the published package and Media Chrome reference. The one substantive hallucination was the fabricated `--media-control-bar-background` CSS variable used in Rung 3; the agent did self-correct after browser inspection showed it had no effect, but the variable was confidently cited in committed code as if it were a real part of the API.
